- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen next 3–5 days’ forecast by 5–15%.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.17) and price is trending down, model underestimates the decline — adjust downward by 3–8% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.1), model often overfits recent volatility — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of sharp drop after peak), model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early days (1–7) when sentiment is positive — reduce first 3–5 days’ forecast by 5–10%.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize the reversal — delay correction until 2–3 days after sentiment shift.
